terms.definition: The shape traced by the tip of $\mathbf{E}$ in time at a fixed point: a line, a circle or an ellipse.
$\mathbf{E}$ oscillates along one fixed line. $\delta=0$ or $180^\circ$.
$\mathbf{E}$ keeps a constant magnitude and turns at $\omega$. $a_x=a_y$, $\delta=\pm90^\circ$.
The general case: the tip of $\mathbf{E}$ traces an ellipse.
Circular polarization that turns the way the fingers of the left hand curl when its thumb points along the direction of travel. $\delta=+90^\circ$ for a wave toward $+z$.
Circular polarization that turns with the right-hand rule about the direction of travel. $\delta=-90^\circ$ for a wave toward $+z$.
Phase of the $y$ component of $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}$ relative to the $x$ component.
$\tan^{-1}(a_y/a_x)$: sets the relative size of the two components.
Angle between the major axis of the polarization ellipse and the $x$ axis.
Sets the shape and handedness of the ellipse: $0$ for linear, $\pm45^\circ$ for circular.
Major axis over minor axis of the polarization ellipse. 1 for circular, infinite for linear.
